summaries.summary: Chatbots have evolved from AIML, handcrafted rules, and information retrieval to neural conversation models and KB-grounded systems, but existing systems do not learn new knowledge during conversations.
KB completion is a binary classification problem over query triples, but existing approaches assume known entities and relations and cannot handle unknown knowledge in conversations.
The paper removes KBC's closed-world assumption, defines open-world knowledge base completion (OKBC), and formulates conversational knowledge learning and inference as interactive OKBC.
User utterances yield true facts and queries; true facts are added to the KB and may enable KBC inference, while query facts with unknown components require OKBC.
OKBC is the core of a conversational knowledge learning engine, and the paper assumes fact/relation extraction, resolution, and related-fact guessing are handled by other sub-systems.

LiLi mimics human interactive reasoning by interleaving processing and interactive actions, retaining acquired facts, and leveraging accumulated knowledge and past inference performances for future learning.
This setting is ideal for NLP applications like dialog and question-answering systems that allow human interaction and require real-time inference.
LiLi extends path-ranking and C-PR from closed-world KBC to OKBC and adopts a compositional vector space model with continual learning capability for prediction.
LiLi formulates dynamic questions, uses acquired supporting facts for inference, is designed in an RL setting, and is evaluated on Freebase and WordNet.
The authors know of no knowledge learning system that learns new knowledge during conversation, so the section discusses other related work.

Existing KB completion, NELL, interactive language learning, question-asking, and dialogue systems lack LiLi's interactive knowledge learning, query-specific strategies, or lifelong prediction-model training.
General lifelong learning work learns only one type of task and is unsuitable for LiLi's interleaving of RL, supervised, and interactive learning.
LiLi combines an RL model for query-specific OKBC inference strategies with a lifelong relation-specific prediction model, improving through user interaction and knowledge retention.
LiLi maps open-world to closed-world by asking users for clues for unknown relations or connecting link queries (CLQs) for unknown entities.
To address KB sparseness, LiLi uses “@-?-@
If users cannot answer MLQs or CLQs, LiLi uses a guessing mechanism to continue inference.
LiLi's Knowledge Store (KS) retains a Knowledge Graph, Relation-Entity Matrix, Task Experience Store using Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), and Incomplete Feature DB.
The RL model learns from unseen states, KS is continuously updated, and the prediction model uses lifelong learning by transferring parameters from similar past tasks.
LiLi uses an Inference Stack to hold query state information, process user clues first, and learn prediction models before inference, transforming OKBC to KBC.
An OKBC query is represented as a data instance containing the query triple, interaction limit, experience list, mode, and feature set before RL-based strategy formulation begins.
Strategy formulation is an inference game where LiLi wins if the relation becomes known and path features are extracted, enabling prediction-model training and inference.
LiLi models strategy formulation as an MDP with 10 binary state variables and 6 actions, using Q-learning with an ε-greedy strategy and rewards for valid actions.
When an unseen state causes repeated invalid actions, LiLi switches to training mode and randomly explores actions through fault-tolerant learning.

Action execution updates the Inference Stack and experience list for invalid actions, while valid actions set the next state, perform operations, monitor interaction limits, and return to the RL model.
LiLi searches KS components, sets state bits, may randomly set bits for unknown or poorly learned relations, and updates KS with clue triples.
LiLi asks the user for a positive clue for an unknown relation and corrupts its source and target once at a time to generate negative instances.
LiLi selects incomplete paths for MLQs using frequency and contextual similarity, and guesses “@-LooselyRelatedTo-@
LiLi asks CLQs to connect unknown entities with the most contextually relevant node from the KB, using contextual relevance computed with word embedding BIBREF39.
LiLi extracts path features, updates the Incomplete Feature DB, trains prediction models with complete features, and monitors requirements to control MLQ interactions.
If LiLi wins an episode, it adds the instance to training, validation, or evaluation buffers based on mode and invokes the prediction model when appropriate.

Lifelong relation prediction trains relation-specific models using 10% of clue instances, an LSTM, cosine similarity, log-likelihood, MCC updates, inverse models, and relation-specific prediction thresholds.
LiLi transfers weights from the most similar past relation using truncated SVD of the Relation-Entity Matrix, or randomly initializes weights when no suitable source exists.
